entry.summary:
In Part 1, we talked about why fetching data directly inside useEffect is a flawed approach — tightly coupling component lifecycle to data-fetching logic, leading to unmanageable side effects, broken UX, and stale state bugs. Can Algorithms Be Ethical? The Hidden Bias in Automated Financial Compliance
entry.summary:
The Shift Toward AI-Driven Compliance
The financial sector faces increasing regulatory scrutiny, making compliance a high-stakes operation. Traditional manual compliance methods are time-consuming, inconsistent, and prone to error. The response has been the development of advanced AI-driven tools that promise real-time monitoring, automated reporting, and predictive analytics. However, while these tools reduce human error, they introduce a new kind of risk—algorithmic bias. When historical data reflects prior discriminatory patterns, the software trained on it may reproduce or amplify them. An algorithm might flag a transaction as suspicious not based on actual risk, but due to flawed or incomplete training data. The bias embedded in automated compliance systems is often unintentional,…
